who_for: A mesh Wi-Fi system is the fix for dead zones in larger or multi-story homes, or homes with thick walls where a single router can't reach every room. Several units work together as one network.
In a small apartment, one good router is usually enough and costs less. Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 only help if your phones and laptops support them and your internet plan is fast.

how_we_picked.label: Coverage
how_we_picked.text: We matched each system's coverage and number of units to realistic home sizes.

how_we_picked.label: Wi-Fi standard
how_we_picked.text: Wi-Fi 6 is the baseline we recommend. Wi-Fi 6E and 7 add less-crowded bands that help in busy buildings with newer devices.

how_we_picked.label: Wired backhaul and ports
how_we_picked.text: Units with Ethernet ports let you connect them with cables for faster, steadier speeds, and plug in desktops or TVs.

how_we_picked.label: Setup and app
how_we_picked.text: A clear app for setup, parental controls, and guest networks matters for everyday use.

how_we_picked.label: Subscriptions
how_we_picked.text: We noted which features require a paid plan, such as advanced security or parental controls.
